title: How the Printing Press Changed the World
paragraphs: For most of history, books were copied by hand, usually by monks or professional writers. Copying a single book could take months, so books were rare, expensive and owned mainly by churches, universities and wealthy families.

In the middle of the fifteenth century, Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith from Mainz in Germany, developed a printing press with movable metal type. Each letter was a small piece of metal that could be arranged, printed and then used again.

This method made it possible to produce hundreds of identical copies quickly. Gutenberg’s most famous work, a Latin Bible, was finished around 1455. Within a few decades, printing workshops had opened in more than two hundred European towns.

As books became cheaper, more people learned to read. Printed pamphlets spread news and religious and political ideas across borders, and scientists could share their discoveries more accurately. Many historians see the printing press as one of the most important inventions ever.
